description: Window cleaning for Westcliff acreage homes near RM 2222 and Loop 360. Pure water, poles reach three stories, exterior glass is $10 per window.
intro: Westcliff is a small acreage subdivision near RM 2222 and Loop 360, with homes on 1.3 to 4 acre lots. CleanzATX cleans windows here with pure water, and Tyler quotes each home himself over text.

paragraphs: Westcliff sits near the corner where RM 2222 meets Loop 360, a spot that feels more remote than the map suggests. Lots run from about 1.3 to 4 acres, and homes were built between 1987 and 2003. Prices land around $800K to $2M, so the section has both original custom houses and ones that have been updated. It is a small neighborhood with no HOA listed, so each owner keeps up their own place. You see long gravel or paved drives, native live oak and cedar, and yards that blend into the hills. Many houses back onto a slope or a wooded gully.
The upside is space and privacy. The downside, for glass, is that nature is always close.

Homes from the late 1980s through the early 2000s often have older frames and screens that have taken a lot of sun. Hard water from sprinklers has had years to bake into the lower panes. Where spotting has set, hard water spot removal is $10 per pane, and pure water cleaning afterward keeps new spots from coming back. Our dual RO, 4 stage system with a DI resin tank gives water near 0 TDS, so cleaned glass dries without a film. Water fed poles reach up to three stories, and tall gable windows on these older plans are common.

Tree cover means spider webs on eaves and leaf litter in tracks. Cedar pollen hits December to February, followed by live oak pollen in March and April. Screens are $5, tracks are $5, and solar screens are $15.

No gate and no HOA make Westcliff simple to book. We text the window count and any driveway notes, pick a time, and show up. On acreage, the 8 ft skid with 200 gallons on board means we can work far from the spigot. Pets and wildlife are normal in the yard, so we ask about dogs ahead of time. Older stucco and stone soak up dirt and algae, and a soft wash, from $0.20 per sq ft with a $400 minimum, makes a visible difference. Gutters, at $1.50 per linear foot for one story and $2.25 for two, are worth adding where oaks drop leaves.
For a 3,500 sq ft home, exterior windows run about $350. Expect around two and a half to three and a half hours outside and about one hour forty five minutes inside.
